title: Fried green tomatoes
subtitle: Cornmeal-crusted slices of unripe tomato, pan-fried until golden
excerpt: Fried green tomatoes are thick slices of unripe green tomato dredged in seasoned cornmeal and pan-fried in a shallow layer of oil until the crust is golden and the tomato is just tender. They are tart and savoury, eaten as a starter or side dish. A classic of the American South.
sourceNotes: Southern American culinary tradition. Fried green tomatoes as a Southern dish is documented in WPA Southern state food surveys and in late nineteenth-century American cookbooks. Edna Lewis, The Taste of Country Cooking (1976), describes fried tomatoes as a summer farmhouse staple.

content.text: Fried green tomatoes are thick slices of unripe tomato, firm and tart, coated in seasoned cornmeal and fried in a hot pan until the crust is crisp and golden and the tomato slices are just tender. They are the best way to use tomatoes that will not ripen before the season ends. A buttermilk dipping sauce alongside is traditional.

items.prepNote: green and firm, not ripe, sliced 1 cm thick

content.text: Set up three shallow bowls. Bowl one: {{plain-flour}} of flour. Bowl two: the 2 beaten eggs mixed with {{buttermilk}} of buttermilk. Bowl three: {{polenta}} of cornmeal mixed with {{paprika-smoked}} of smoked paprika, cayenne, salt, and pepper.
Pat the tomato slices dry. Dredge each one in flour, dip in the egg-buttermilk mix, then press firmly into the seasoned cornmeal to coat.

Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the coated tomato slices in a single layer for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden. Drain on a rack. Season immediately with salt.

items.symptom: Crust falling off in the oil
items.cause: Tomato slices wet, or coating not pressed firmly.
items.fix: Pat the slices completely dry before coating. Press the cornmeal on firmly.
The oil must be properly hot before the tomatoes go in. Test with a small pinch of cornmeal: it should sizzle.

content.text: A dipping sauce of mayonnaise, hot sauce, and a pinch of smoked paprika is the standard accompaniment. Serve alongside devilled eggs and pimento cheese for a Southern starter spread. The same cornmeal coating works on aubergine slices.

Fried green tomatoes are a Southern summer staple: a way to use the last unripe tomatoes before the frost, or the ones that fell from the vine too early. They were a farmhouse regular long before the 1991 film of the same name made them famous and briefly outpaced supply at farmers' markets.
